recommendation_summary: The reply recommends adding a hosted dead man's switch (for example healthchecks.io): the script pings it on success, and if no ping arrives by about 03:30 the service emails the user.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need to be alerted when nightly-sync fails, without reading logs — that's your own stated requirement, not a style preference.
labels.Deleted: Central log aggregation on Synology in Docker (Pieter Levels style) — it still requires you to go look at logs, which you said you won't do, and it doesn't fix the actual gap (failure before the job's own email step).
labels.Bottleneck: The job crashes at startup before it reaches the email call, so the only existing signal (the summary email) never fires on failure — that's a missing failure signal, not a missing log store.
labels.Checked myself: You told me cron on edna is the only scheduler, the email is sent by the script itself at the end of a successful run, and nothing else currently watches this job.

note: The reply recommends one hosted heartbeat alert, explicitly rejects the Synology/Docker log stack, and its Checked myself line only restates facts the user gave.
